query: Closed, Even to Me The headmistress sets a small wooden box on the table and opens it. It is empty. "Close it," she says, "so that it stays closed. To anyone. Even to me." She sits down across from you with her hands folded. "That is Seal." Seal it as tight as you can It takes everything you have and the rest of the hour. The headmistress tries the lid with one finger, then two, then not at all. "Good," she says. You feel scraped hollow until supper. Ask what she keeps sealed "Many things," she says, "for good reasons." She doesn't say more, and you seal the box with that sitting in your stomach. It holds. She doesn't try it.
